title: Quantisation of Abstract Data Types
authors: Mingsheng Ying, Zhicheng Zhang, Kean Chen
abstract: In this paper, we introduce a notion of abstract quantum data type within the framework of universal algebra. This notion provides an algebraic foundation for describing data abstraction in quantum programming. We formally define a quantisation of classical data types and show that their equational specifications can be soundly lifted to the quantum setting. Two standard quantisation methods for classical functions, namely the bit oracle and the phase oracle, arise as special cases of this general construction. We illustrate the framework with applications to quantum arrays and quantum error-correcting codes, showing how they can be understood through the lens of data-type quantisation. We further establish conditions under which quantisation preserves structural relationships and constructions of classical data types, including embeddings, isomorphisms, and products.
summary: This paper introduces a novel algebraic framework to define abstract quantum data types, extending classical universal algebra techniques to the quantum domain. It formalizes the 'quantization' of data type specifications, providing a rigorous mathematical tool for quantum programming. This work is significant for building robust, abstract quantum algorithms independent of specific hardware implementations.
main_problem: To establish an algebraic foundation for data abstraction in quantum programming by defining and quantizing abstract data types.
main_result: The paper formally defines abstract quantum data types using universal algebra and proves that classical data type specifications can be soundly lifted to the quantum setting.
method: The approach uses universal algebra to define quantum signatures and algebras, modeling quantum terms as quantum circuit formulas evaluated on Hilbert spaces.
model_or_system: The model is an abstract quantum algebraic framework where data types are represented by quantum sorts, and operations are represented by unitary gates acting on tensor product Hilbert spaces.
key_observables: State overlaps, inner products, and the equality of quantum circuit evaluations (LHS = RHS) are used to verify algebraic identities.
important_parameters: The structure of the quantum gates (unitary operators) and the initial quantum states (pure states) are central.
main_assumptions: The framework assumes that quantum operations are unitary and that the focus is on pure states, though generalizations are mentioned.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first defining the quantum algebraic structure, then defining quantum terms and equations, and finally proving the validity of structural preservation (embeddings, isomorphisms) by verifying key equations.
why_interesting: It provides a rigorous mathematical formalism for handling data structures in quantum computation, which is crucial for developing hardware-agnostic quantum algorithms.
